capitals.name: Möng Mao (Ruili valley)
capitals.note: Core in the Nam Mao (Ruili) river basin, 'Selan was the most frequently used' of its capitals; coordinates are those of Ruili, approximate. The capital fell in 1442.

capitals.name: Möng Yang (Mohnyin)
capitals.note: After 1442 Si Renfa 'fled to Möng Yang' and the royal family moved west of the Irrawaddy to Möng Yang; the Confederation of 1527 was 'led by the state of Mohnyin' (Ava page). Identifying Möng Yang with Mohnyin is my reading; Mohnyin fell to Bayinnaung on 6 March 1557.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1287-1293: 'Shan political power increased after the Mongols overran Pagan in 1287' and the page has the first large Shan state in the Burma area (Möng Kawng) founded in 1215 and Möng Nai in 1223. Cliopatria's first shape starts in 1294; the extent of 1287-1293 is not on the page and is bridged with the 1294 outline.

correction.text: the 1294 outline, the Shan principalities round the Irrawaddy valley

keyframe_review.note: 293,250 km2: all of Kachin, the Shan plateau, northern Sagaing, the Chin hills and 106 cells of Yunnan, no overlap with the outline of any of sixteen neighbouring Cliopatria states (checked cell by cell). The page gives no area; it describes the Shan states as 'dominat[ing] much of northern and eastern Burma' after 1287 and the Pinya page as 'the arc surrounding the Irrawaddy valley'.
Three cells more than 1294; the Pinya and Sagaing pages show nothing that moved the Shan frontier in 1326 (Sagaing's secession from Pinya in 1325 is Burmese land).
Ten cells more than 1326. The 1364 sack of Sagaing and Pinya by Möng Mao added no Shan land: Thado Minbya 'seized Pinya' in September 1364 and founded Ava in 1365.

297,723 km2, the largest of the early outlines (9 more Yunnan cells). The Mong Mao page has Si Lunfa 'decided to submit to Ming authority' in 1382 and be promoted in August 1384; the ledger records the Ming wars of 1385-1388 as a contest.

274,022 km2: Cliopatria drops 93 Yunnan cells in 1385. The Mong Mao page does not support that: Si Lunfa surrendered only in 1388, invaded Ava in 1393, was deposed in 1397 and restored in 1398, and Si Renfa still held 'Möng Mao's capital' until 1442 (taken again 1444; 'Möng Mao was finally defeated in 1444', Shan States page). After Si Lunfa's death in 1399 the Ming 'split Möng Mao's territory into smaller states and established 13 new states under its control', yet the 1442 Burmese inscription lists 21 states under Si Renfa: so Yunnan stays in the outline until 1444. Years 1385-1428; no infobox area to compare.

Same outline as Cliopatria's 1429 shape.

correction.text: the Shan outline without the Yunnan lands

keyframe_review.note: 273,899 km2: three Sagaing cells fewer than 1429; nothing on the pages opened.

273,677 km2, unchanged in extent. Years 1502-1526: the Confederation of Shan States 'sacked Ava' in 1527 ('Start of Shan period: 14 March 1527'), two years before Cliopatria's shape grows; new keyframe 1527.

New keyframe, 1527-1528: 'In 1527, the Confederation of Shan States, led by the state of Mohnyin in alliance with Prome, sacked Ava' and 'ruled much of Upper Burma'; the Shan page: 'ruled Upper Burma until 1555'. The land is Cliopatria's 1529 outline; Cliopatria's Ava row runs to 1528 and double-covers these two years (ava-kingdom should end in 1526 or 1527).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1529 outline, which adds Ava's 114,395 km2 (Shan 134 cells, Sagaing 128, Mandalay 74, Magway 70)

keyframe_review.note: 387,847 km2 for 1529-1532 as drawn (+407 cells over 1502, all Ava's land). Not on the page: an area. From 1533 the Prome land is added (new keyframe 1533): the Confederation 'extended its authority down to Prome (Pyay) in 1533'.

New keyframe, 1533-1541: 'The enlarged Confederation extended its authority down to Prome (Pyay) in 1533' (the First Toungoo Empire page: the Confederation had 'by 1533 ... defeated its erstwhile ally Prome'). Cliopatria keeps Prome as its own row to 1546 and gives the Shan outline nothing; the Prome sidebar of the Toungoo page reads 1482-1542, so the hold is taken to end in 1542.
387,527 km2, nine cells fewer than 1529 (Kayah, Shan). Years 1542-1544: Prome out, Toungoo not yet at Pagan ('seized up to Pagan (Bagan)' from the Confederation 'by 1545').

New keyframe, 1545-1546: Cliopatria takes 111 cells (Magway 68, Mandalay 34, Sagaing 8) from the Confederation only in 1547, but the Toungoo page has it 'seized up to Pagan (Bagan) ... by 1545' (the Toungoo-Ava War of 1538-45 is linked, not described).

correction.text: unchanged outline, holding from 1547 to January 1555 only: 'In January 1555, King Bayinnaung of the Taungoo dynasty conquered Ava' (infobox 'Toungoo conquest: 22 January 1555'); Ava's land leaves with the ledger's 1555 loss and the 1556 outline applies from then

keyframe_review.note: 356,870 km2, with Ava and the Chindwin country still Shan until Ava fell on 22 January 1555 ('In 1555, Upper Burma fell to the southern forces').

273,864 km2: Ava's land is gone (Magway, Sagaing, Mandalay) and 135 Shan cells with it. Bayinnaung took the cis-Salween Shan states 'by March 1557' (Mohnyin 6 March, Mogaung 11 March), Kengtung submitted before the invasion of 16 December 1562 and by 1563 he had 'at least nominal suzerainty over the Chinese Shan states'; the outline from 1557 is the Shan principalities as Toungoo vassals (infobox 'Shan States 1557-1581'), which first-toungoo-empire should carry as vassal tint. Cliopatria ends the row in 1563.

ledger.note: 1287: the Shan principalities rise as Pagan falls. 'Shan political power increased after the Mongols overran Pagan in 1287', and the Shan states are 'independence from the Pagan and Dali kingdoms in the 13th century' in the infobox. The page gives a date for the rise, not a founding of a joint state, and no extent: Cliopatria's 1294 outline is used.

ledger.note: 1388: Si Lunfa surrenders to the Ming ('Si Lunfa surrendered in 1388') after a larger punitive expedition; he invaded Ava in 1393, was deposed in 1397 and restored in 1398.

1444: the Ming take the Yunnan lands of Möng Mao. 'Möng Mao was finally defeated in 1444' and its royal family moved west of the Irrawaddy to Möng Yang; on the Mong Mao page the third campaign took the capital again and the core region was 'partitioned into Möng Wan (Longchuan)'.

ledger.note: 1449: the fourth campaign ends in a peace treaty with Silu, a son of Si Renfa, and 'a boundary stone was set up on the Irrawaddy'.

ledger.note: 14 March 1527: the Confederation of Shan States sacks Ava. 'In 1527, the Confederation of Shan States, led by the state of Mohnyin in alliance with Prome, sacked Ava'; 'The Confederation placed nominal kings on the Ava throne and ruled much of Upper Burma'; infobox 'Start of Shan period: 14 March 1527', Thohanbwa king 1527-1542.
1533: the Confederation takes Prome: 'The enlarged Confederation extended its authority down to Prome (Pyay) in 1533 by defeating their erstwhile ally Prome Kingdom', its ally of 1527.
1542: Prome leaves the Confederation's hold. The Toungoo page's sidebar reads 'Prome kingdom 1482-1542' and gives no event; who took it is not on the page.

1545: Toungoo pushes the Confederation back to Pagan. The First Toungoo Empire page has it 'seized up to Pagan (Bagan)' from the Confederation 'by 1545'; the Toungoo-Ava War (1538-45) is linked but not described. Cliopatria draws the loss in 1547.

The saophas stay as vassals.

notes:
Cliopatria's Shan States is one row for a ring of principalities (Möng Mao, Möng Yang/Mohnyin, Mogaung, Hsenwi, Hsipaw, Kengtung ...) with no cell shared with its sixteen neighbouring Cliopatria outlines; it is kept as one state, as the brief says Cliopatria lacks the Shan states as separate polities, and a gap-filler could split Möng Mao (Yunnan, to 1444) and the Confederation (1527-1555) into their own dossiers.

Corrections to Cliopatria: (1) the 93 Yunnan cells dropped in 1385 are kept to 1444 (Mong Mao page), with a new 1444 keyframe; (2) the 1527 sack of Ava starts two years before the 1529 shape (new 1527 keyframe; ava-kingdom's Cliopatria row ends 1528 and double-covers 1527-1528); (3) Prome 1533 (Shan States page) is added though Cliopatria keeps Prome separate to 1546, ending in 1542 on the Toungoo page's sidebar only (confidence 1); (4) the 1545 loss up to Pagan is two years before the 1547 shape. The row ends 1563, not at the 1557 subjugation: the principalities go on as Toungoo's vassals; the Federated Shan States of 1922 are not covered.

Open items: infobox gives no area ('Area: not given'); capitals are the strongest principality's seat (the Shan states had no common capital; the infobox 'Taunggyi' is a modern town, not used); Möng Yang is identified with Mohnyin by me; 1287 start is the page's 'Mongols overran Pagan in 1287' and the pagan-kingdom dossier's 1287 loss to shan-states; the extent 1287-1293 is bridged. The Dali Kingdom (infobox predecessor) has no Cliopatria row. Hsenwi/Kengtung/Mong Nai etc. were not opened separately (page budget 5: Shan States, Mong Mao, Kingdom of Ava, Bayinnaung, First Toungoo Empire; Pinya and Sagaing pages opened for those dossiers are cited for 1364 only). first-toungoo-empire should carry the vassal_start events for the Shan states (Hsipaw 25 January 1557, Mohnyin 6 March, Mogaung 11 March, Mone November 1557, Hsenwi 26 July 1558, Kengtung 16 December 1562, Chinese Shan states 1563) and ming-dynasty the Mong Mao tusi relation (1382, August 1384).
